AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The associations between Chlamydophila (Chlamydia) pneumonia infection and chronic asthma or bronchial hyper-responsiveness (BHR) have been inconclusive.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: We aimed to determine the association between C. pneumonia infection and asthma as well as BHR in the adult Thai population.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHOD
AbstractText.content: This nested case-control study retrieved the data from a nation-wide Respiratory Health Survey (2001-02) in the adult population (age 20-44 year) in Thailand. Each subject underwent questionnaire interview, spirometry, bronchoprovocative test, skin prick test for common aeroallergens and venous blood collection. Subjects with BHR (n = 79) including those with asthma (n = 52), were randomly selected as cases. Subjects without BHR or asthma were also randomly selected as the control (n = 137). We used the stored serums for the C. pneumonia serologic assay including IgA, IgG and IgM by microimmunofluorescence (MIF) technique.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There is no significant relationship between chronic Chlamydia infection (IgG > or = 1:512 and IgA > or = 1:40) and BHR or asthma. Higher IgM was found in subjects with BHR when compared with the control group (p = 0.04). The IgM titer > or = 1:10 was associated with BHR with borderline significance (odds ratio 1.98; 95% CI 0.98-4.00; p = 0.05). Logistic regression analysis revealed no evidence of confounding effects for age, sex and atopy. However mite allergy seems to be an effect modifier of the relationship between the recent Chlamydia infection and BHR.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The present study does not support the hypothesis about the association between persistent C. pneumonia infection and chronic asthma. However the recent infection may be related with bronchial hyper-responsiveness particularly in those without allergy to house dust mite.
